messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable game inspired by FLYVIBE, featuring a new level, a flying supercar, one new mechanic, a fresh challenge, polished visuals, and a start page leading into gameplay.

## Requirements
- Deliver a playable game without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Aim for a “4k graphics” visual feel and a high-quality overall experience.
- Include a starting page and main game.
- Save any screenshots used for checks as small JPEGs at no more than 1280px wide; inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Created “SKYLINE // Afterburn,” a neon-city flying-supercar arcade runner.
- New mechanic: spend/recharge phase charge to pass through hazards; added boost and collectible ion rings.
- Implemented in a standalone HTML file with a responsive canvas-rendered scene and touch controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a start screen, HUD, pause/end screens, keyboard and touch controls, score/best persistence, city visuals, flying car, rings, hazards, boost, and phase mechanic in `index.html`.
- Installed Chromium and opened the game in Playwright.
- Extracted JavaScript and passed `node --check /tmp/afterburn.js`.

### Active
- Fix and verify the game’s runtime JavaScript after the browser reported `ReferenceError: update is not defined`.

### Blocked
- Browser check was not rerun after editing the script to address the runtime error.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` around the end of the `<script>` and ensure `update`, input handlers, `spawnWave`, and `frame` all appear inside the IIFE and script tags.
2. Run `node --check` on the extracted script, then reload `http://localhost:3002` and verify the start screen and gameplay in Playwright.
3. Check browser console for further errors and capture a small JPEG screenshot if useful.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: all game markup, styles, and JavaScript; currently contains the in-progress implementation.

## Important Context
- Playwright initially reported `ReferenceError: update is not defined` at `frame`; inspection showed the `</script></body></html>` tags appeared before `keyMap` and the update/input functions. The latest edit removed those premature closing tags, but the browser has not yet been reloaded to confirm the correction.
- Changes are uncommitted.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, polished, playable game inspired by FLYVIBE: a neon-city flying-supercar runner with a new mechanic, challenge, start page, and main game.

## Requirements
- Aim for a “4k graphics” visual feel and strong overall quality.
- Deliver a playable game without clarifying questions.
- Save any screenshots used for checks as JPEGs no wider than 1280px; inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Created “SKYLINE // Afterburn,” a neon-city arcade flight runner.
- New mechanic: spend/recharge phase charge to pass through hazards; added boost and collectible ion rings.
- Implemented as a standalone, responsive canvas-rendered `index.html` with keyboard and touch controls.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added start, pause, and end screens; HUD; score/best persistence; city visuals; flying car; rings; hazards; boost; phase; and mobile controls.
- Fixed the misplaced script closing tags and restored the IIFE closure.
- Extracted JavaScript and verified it with `node --check /tmp/afterburn.js`.
- Reloaded in Playwright: the `update is not defined` error is resolved; only a missing favicon 404 remains in the console.

### Active
- Fix the CSS parse error: `.screen` is being computed as `position: static`, and the start button is outside the viewport. The `.vignette` background declaration appears to be missing a closing `)` for its final `linear-gradient(...)`, preventing subsequent CSS rules from applying.
- Recheck start page and gameplay in Playwright after fixing CSS.

### Blocked
- Browser interaction verification is blocked until the CSS parsing/layout issue is corrected.

## Next Move
1. Add the missing closing parenthesis in the `.vignette` background declaration in `index.html`.
2. Reload `http://localhost:3002`; verify `.screen` is positioned correctly and the start button is visible/clickable.
3. Start a run and check gameplay plus the browser console; save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot if useful.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: all game markup, styles, and JavaScript; contains the CSS issue to fix.

## Important Context
- Playwright’s click on `#startBtn` timed out because it reported the button outside the viewport. Evaluation showed `.screen` had computed `position: static`; stylesheet rules stopped after `.vignette`.
- Changes are uncommitted.
